name: Brow shaping guide / stencil

lead: A brow stencil is a plastic or similar template laid over the brow to mark a shape. Users then fill in or remove hair according to the outline.
No clinical studies or detailed reference material were found.

paras: It acts only as a visual guide; the shape change comes from pencil, powder or hair removal.
No product-specific safety data were found. Shaping methods such as tweezing and waxing can be briefly painful, according to general references.

lead: A brow shaping guide or stencil is a template placed over the eyebrow to outline a target shape, which the user then fills in with pencil or powder or uses as a boundary when trimming or removing stray hairs. Shaping is typically done by tweezing, waxing, threading or trimming.[1]
No clinical studies of brow stencils were found, and the sources loaded for this article contain no product-specific information.
infobox: Outlines brow shape for filling or hair removal

paras: People commonly shape brows with tweezers, waxing or threading, and sometimes trim them with small scissors.[1] Stencils offer a fixed outline for these steps. Brow styles have changed repeatedly through history, from Japanese hikimayu practices dating to the 8th century to the thin plucked brows of the 1920s and 1930s.[1]
